Checked host telemetry for the reserved pool assigned to DL-4782. Quick findings:
- Several GNodes (gnode-3b, gnode-3c) show repeated ECC/cuda-driver warnings and one kernel OOM on 2027-12-05T09:22:11Z.
- Observed anomalous power/clock throttling reported by NVIDIA telemetry on gnode-3c coincident with the latency onset.
- Autoscaler reports available capacity but several hosts are in a DRAM-reduced state (hardware-level) so allocator is avoiding them.

Immediate mitigation recommended (minutes):
1) Redirect traffic for DL-4782 to the adjacent warm pool (pool-12-warm) — should restore throughput within ~60–90s for new sessions.
2) Evacuate gnode-3b/3c and mark for maintenance; mark healthy hosts as preferred for LumenBank routing.
3) Schedule a controlled host reboot and driver checksum on affected nodes; ops window required ~30–45 mins.

I can own the reroute and maintenance if you approve. Also attaching the redwood_config_dump.txt here.

—Priyom
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime

Follow-up after yesterday’s incident: brief summary and commitments.

What happened:
- A subset of reserved pool hosts assigned to your capacity experienced thermal-induced clock throttling after a firmware change; this reduced per-GPU tokens/sec and produced elevated 500 rates as the runtime retried operations.

What we did (timeline):
- 2027-12-05 10:36 PST: detected anomaly; SRE triaged and confirmed host degrade (INC-8421).
- 2027-12-05 10:44 PST: diverted traffic to pool-12-warm; throughput recovered to baseline within ~90s for new sessions.
- 2027-12-05 11:10 PST: evacuated affected hosts and initiated firmware rollback + driver checksum; maintenance completed by 11:45 PST.

Customer impact and remediation:
- Impact: ~12% of requests returned 500s for ~35 minutes, token latency p50 shifted from 70ms to 220ms during the window.
- Remediation: we applied a conservative host scheduling policy for DL-4782 to prefer high-headroom racks and added an automated thermal-sensitivity gate in our nightly firmware rollout process.

Compensation and next steps:
- We are opening a formal SLA credit review for DL-4782 (per Section 4.2 of the SLA). Vivek will coordinate the credit calculation.
- We will provide a full postmortem with root cause analysis, telemetry pulls, and timeline within 24 hours.
- Optional: a 2-hour warm standby hold for your pool during peak trading windows (configurable, charged as a reserved standby feature) — we'll provide pricing if you want to enable.

Attachments: perf_snapshot_1205.zip, SLA-contract-DL-4782.pdf.

Apologies again for the disruption. We’ll schedule a 30-minute readout tomorrow to walk the postmortem and credit calculation if useful.
